question: Do the varying CameraRecoil.IdleSpring fields on the selected 12 weapons support a source-backed comparison of visual settling that the Analyzer does not show?

sourceFacts.comparison: Site 0.6695 equals the pinned raw f32 and the named GS_HK433.Recoil.Zoomed.RecoilAmount registry scalar.

inference: In the selected sample, 10 of the 12 named IdleSpring fields vary: four constant/damping fields and six switch-time fields; IdleSpringExponent and IdleSpringExponentZoomed are 30.0 on all 12 weapons. This supports a source-value comparison of raw tuples. The numbers do not establish which weapon visually settles faster or how long settling takes.
unresolved: The serialized IdleSpring consumer, activation state and camera output channel are not identified.
No source equation maps the named scalar values to visual displacement or settling time; units for the values are unresolved.
The zoomed/unzoomed switch-time parameters do not establish transition interpolation or native composition.

The cached registry binding report marks its registry layout provisional. The 11 available per-weapon associations are exact child/hash rows and scalar matches, while BREN3 has no registry anchor and was read directly through its pinned descriptor-resolved CameraRecoil object.
siteImpact: The Analyzer currently models ballistic recoil through recoil.amount * amountMult^amountExp and separate decay inputs (decFactor, decExp, decTimeExp, decOffset). The 12 weapons support a side-by-side comparison of serialized CameraRecoil.IdleSpring parameter tuples only. This evidence does not support a visual-settling speed or duration, angular or time units, a spring equation, a rank, or a user-facing feature proposal. Before proposing such a feature, trace the runtime consumer and equation that map these scalars to the camera output, including units and zoom/transition activation and composition.
